title: The Destruction of the Pocket
subtitle: The defeat of the Soviet Southwestern Front
author: R.G. Cruise
phase: III — The Battle for Strategic Objectives
summary: The principal Kiev encirclement battle reached its conventional endpoint, while isolated resistance and the treatment of prisoners require separate evidence.
outlineTopics: The course of the encirclement after September 16.
German efforts to reduce separated Soviet formations.
The attempts by Soviet armies and smaller groups to break out.
The fate of the Southwestern Front command.
The death of Mikhail Kirponos during the breakout fighting.
The collapse of organized resistance within the principal encirclement.
The destruction, dispersal, or escape of Soviet formations.
German claims concerning prisoners and captured equipment.
Differences between contemporary German figures and later historical estimates.
The consequences for Soviet defensive operations farther east.
German operational losses and logistical difficulties.
The position of Army Group South after the battle.
The significance of the Kiev victory for German strategic planning.
Whether the victory advanced or complicated the wider objectives of Barbarossa.
The consequences for the occupied Ukrainian population.
researchStatus: Editorial outline and date association established. Full researched narrative, claim-level citations and the dated military situation remain to be written and reconstructed.
referenceMapStatus: Candidate German General Staff plate from the supplied chronological sequence. The plate title/date, operational content and reuse conditions have not been independently verified for digitisation.
chronologyNotes: 26 September is a conventional endpoint of the principal battle, not proof that every isolated unit ceased fighting. Prisoner figures require attributed categories.
